verses.text: So if there is any encouragement in Christ, any comfort from love, any sharing in the Spirit, any tenderness or compassion,
then make my joy complete: be united in purpose, share the same love, and be one in heart and mind.
Don't act out of selfish ambition or vanity. Instead, be humble and consider others more important than yourselves.
Each of you should look out not only for your own interests but also for the interests of others.
Adopt the same attitude as Christ Jesus:
Though he existed in God's form, he didn't treat equality with God as something to exploit.
Instead, he emptied himself, taking the form of a servant and becoming like human beings.
When he appeared as a human, he humbled himself and obeyed all the way to death—even death on a cross.
Because of this, God raised him to the highest place and gave him the name above every name,
so that at Jesus' name every knee will bow—in heaven, on earth, and under the earth—
and every tongue will confess that Jesus Christ is Lord, to the glory of God the Father.
So then, my dear friends, just as you always obeyed—not only when I was with you, but even more now that I'm away—keep living out your salvation with reverence and humility.
God is the one working in you, giving you both the desire and the ability to do what pleases him.
Do everything without grumbling or arguing,
so you can be blameless and sincere, God's children without fault in a twisted and crooked generation. Then you'll shine among them like stars in the sky,
as you hold firmly to the word of life. Then on Christ's day I'll have reason to be proud that I didn't run or work for nothing.
Even if I'm being poured out like a drink offering over the sacrifice and service of your faith, I'm glad and rejoice with all of you.
In the same way, you should be glad and rejoice with me.
I hope in the Lord Jesus to send Timothy to you soon, so I'll be encouraged when I hear how you're doing.
I have no one else like him who will genuinely care about your situation.
Everyone else looks out for their own interests, not for those of Jesus Christ.
But you know Timothy's proven character. He served with me in the work of the Good News like a son working alongside his father.
So I hope to send him as soon as I know what will happen with me.
And I'm confident in the Lord that I'll come soon too.
I thought it necessary to send Epaphroditus back to you. He's my brother, co-worker, and fellow soldier, and he is your messenger who helped meet my needs.
He has been longing to see you all and was distressed because you heard he was sick.
He really was sick—almost to the point of death. But God showed mercy to him, and not only to him but also to me, so I wouldn't have one sorrow piled on another.
So I'm sending him back as soon as I can, so you'll be glad to see him again and I'll have less sorrow.
Welcome him in the Lord with great joy, and honor people like him.
He came close to death for the work of Christ, risking his life to make up for the help you couldn't give me in person.
